# Corrections Report

Simply-Fit, internship version (ZIP `Simply-Fit-main-2`) to M.Tech version.

Every row describes a change that was actually made and how it was checked. "Evidence" numbers come from running the frozen original code (`src/legacy/`, byte-identical to the ZIP) in `experiments/audit_original.py` (output: `results/audit/audit_original.json`). "Result" numbers on accuracy come from simulated evaluation data (`EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md`); they are not real-world validation. Numbers in this file are filled in from those result files by `python -m experiments.build_report`.

## A. Energy-balance estimation

| Original issue | Evidence in code | Correction implemented | Validation performed | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1. The headline accuracy claim was circular.** README: "recovers realized energy balance, median error 8 kcal/day". | `scripts/build_notebooks.py` (notebook 02 cell): `realized = np.polyfit(range(len(w)), w, 1)[0] * 7700`. The "truth" was a straight-line fit to the same noisy readings, not the simulator's balance. | New simulator stores the true daily balance (`src/simulation.py`); all accuracy is scored against it. The claim was removed from the README. | Audit A11: an instrumented copy of the original generator (verified to reproduce its logs exactly) exposes the true balance. | Against that circular reference: 7.3 kcal/day. Against the true simulated balance: 11.0 kcal/day median, 32.9 at the 90th percentile. The original was in fact accurate on its own easy data (90 days, independent noise, no gaps); the method of checking was wrong and the setting was unrepresentative. |
| **2. Smoothing before regression shrinks the slope.** | `src/ml_engine.py` `estimate_calorie_balance`: regression is run on `ewm(span=7, adjust=False)` output, which starts at the first reading and then lags. | Regression runs on raw readings (`src/energy_balance.py`, Huber fit). No smoothing step. | Audit A1 on a noise-free -550 kcal/day line; unit test `test_known_linear_trend_recovered_exactly_without_noise` (12 cases). | Original research module returned -448.0 at 14 days (18.5% error), -517.6 at 28 days, -550.7 at 90 days. Corrected code returns -550.0 at every length. On noisy data this shrinkage lowers average error at 14 days and under-reports sustained deficits; see `EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md` section 6. |
| **3. Two different estimators in one project.** | `app/streamlit_app.py` lines 402-420 re-implemented EWMA, Isolation Forest and regression, and regressed on anomaly-replaced *raw* data; `src/ml_engine.py` regressed on *smoothed* data. The app's displayed number never came from the tested module. | One implementation in `src/energy_balance.py`; app, coach, experiments and tests all import it. `src/ml_engine.py` is now a thin wrapper. | Audit A2; `test_app_has_no_private_copies_of_statistical_code`; `test_full_workflow_displays_exactly_the_backend_estimate`; `test_run_pipeline_agrees_with_shared_core`. | On 300 identical 28-day logs the two original paths disagreed by 48.9 kcal/day on average (maximum 193.6). Now the app displays exactly the backend value (tests pass). |
| **4. Missed days were treated as consecutive days.** | Both original estimators use `np.arange(len(log))` as the time axis; the app stored a bare list of floats with no dates. | Readings carry real day indices; missed days are `None`; regression is against actual days (`validate_weight_log`, `estimate_energy_balance`). Text entry accepts `-` for a missed day; CSV upload accepts a date column. | Audit A3 (noise-free line with days removed); tests `test_missing_days_do_not_bias_the_slope`, `test_explicit_irregular_days_equal_grid_with_gaps`; simulated sweeps. | Original with 20% / 40% of days missing: -26.6% / -64.7% error on a noise-free line. ## B. Anomaly detection

| Original issue | Evidence in code | Correction implemented | Validation performed | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **9. Isolation Forest contamination fixed at 0.1.** | `IsolationForest(contamination=0.1, random_state=42)` in both estimators: about 10% of readings are flagged whatever the data. | Isolation Forest removed from the estimation path. Huber regression down-weights readings far from the trend, by an amount that depends on how far they are. | Audit A4 on error-free Gaussian data; `test_clean_gaussian_data_flags_few_readings`. | Original flagged 10.7% of readings on data with no errors. Corrected code marks under 4% as "unusual" on the same kind of data and down-weights rather than removes them. |
| **10. Flagged readings were overwritten with lagging EWMA values.** | `clean_weights = np.where(flags, smoothed, weight_log)`: a measurement is replaced by a value that trails the trend. | No reading is ever replaced or deleted. | `test_no_reading_is_ever_replaced_or_removed`, `test_gross_errors_do_not_move_robust_estimate_much`; gross-error sweep. | 10% gross errors, 28 days: error 170 (original app), 198 (original research module), 139 kcal/day (corrected). |
| **11. Use of future observations.** Investigated; **partly confirmed**. | The EWMA is causal: no look-ahead. The Isolation Forest is fitted on the whole log, so which past readings are "anomalies" can change when a new reading arrives. | Trailing-window estimates use only readings up to the day they describe. | Audit A4; `test_rolling_estimates_never_use_future_readings`; `test_tracking_rows_use_only_data_up_to_each_day`. | In 17% of test logs, at least one past flag changed after a single new reading. No leakage was found in any accuracy figure. |
| **12. Was Isolation Forest worth keeping?** | Not assumed either way. | Compared original, original-with-real-days, EWMA-only, least squares, Theil-Sen and Huber on identical data. | `EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md` sections 5 and 6. | It gave no benefit in any condition tested. Reported honestly: on clean, complete logs the original app is as accurate as the corrected method (127 vs 130 kcal/day at 28 days). |

## C. Uncertainty

| Original issue | Evidence in code | Correction implemented | Validation performed | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **13. The "95% CI" was not a 95% interval.** | `kcal_per_day_ci95` uses the classical slope formula on residuals of the already-smoothed series. The docstring admitted it was "anti-conservative" without measuring by how much. | Interval computed on raw readings with an AR(1) sandwich estimator on actual day gaps, small-sample-corrected autocorrelation, t distribution with effective sample size. Classical, Newey-West and block-bootstrap alternatives implemented and compared. | Audit A5; tests against `statsmodels` (`test_classical_se_matches_statsmodels_ols`, `test_hac_se_matches_statsmodels_newey_west`, `test_huber_matches_statsmodels_rlm`); coverage on simulated truth. | Original coverage in the audit: 42% (independent noise) and 38% (persistent noise). On evaluation simulations: original 30%, classical 72%, Newey-West 74%, block bootstrap 69%, adopted method 86%. **Still below 95%**; the app labels the range "approximate" and states this. |
| **14. Three uncertainties were not distinguished.** | One interval, attached to the kcal figure; forecast shown as a bare line. | Code and interface separate: trend-slope interval (kg/week), energy-equivalent interval (kcal/day, excludes uncertainty in 7700), and a prediction interval for future readings. | `test_prediction_interval_reflects_scatter_and_is_wider_than_trend_ci`, `test_prediction_interval_is_empirically_calibrated_on_ar1_noise`. | Forecast band coverage on evaluation simulations: 83% against a nominal 80%. |

## Breaking changes

- `src.ml_engine.run_pipeline` returns `status`, `label`, `reliability` and may return `kcal_per_day = None`; `r_squared`, `food_adjustment_kcal` and `activity_adjustment_kcal` are removed. `ewma_filter`, `detect_anomalies` and `estimate_calorie_balance` now live only in `src/legacy/ml_engine_v1.py`.
- `src.lstm_forecaster.forecast` defaults to the recent-level method; `create_sequences` and `_linear_extrapolate` exist only in the legacy copy. The optional LSTM is a new file, `models/simply_fit_lstm_v2.keras`; the internship model file is kept for the re-evaluation.
- The app's weight log is a daily grid that may contain `None`; the log-entry page no longer starts with values.
- The notebooks are the internship-era record and were not re-run (`notebooks/README.md`).

## Not done

- No real-world data were used; everything quantitative is simulation.
- The confidence interval is better calibrated than before and still below its nominal level.
- The five internship notebooks were not re-executed.
- The guideline texts' sources were not verified.
- The Gemini (LLM) coach path was not exercised: no API key was available in the test environment. Only the deterministic template path is tested.
- The live deployment URL in the old README was not checked or updated.
